"THE CELESTIAL DRAGON

COMPLETE GAME DESIGN DOCUMENT (GDD)

Version: 1.0
Genre: Eastern Fantasy Action RPG / Real-Time Strategy
Perspective: Third-Person
World: Open World
Combat: Real-Time Action Combat + Tactical Army Command
Single Player: Yes
Primary Focus: Exploration, Character Progression, Martial Arts, Bloodline Awakening, Companions, Army Management, and Large-Scale Warfare.

---

1. GAME VISION

The Celestial Dragon is an open-world Eastern Fantasy Action RPG combined with real-time strategy elements.

Players control Je-un, a young man who unknowingly carries the bloodline of the legendary Celestial Dragon Clan.

The player explores a vast world, learns martial arts, discovers ancient secrets, recruits companions, builds an army, and gradually awakens the power of the Celestial Dragon.

The game combines three major experiences:

1. Personal combat and character development.
2. Exploration and discovery in a large fantasy world.
3. Strategic command of companions and large armies.

The main character must become powerful through experience, training, exploration, and difficult decisions.

---

2. WORLD AND LORE

2.1 The Five Major Races

Humans

Humans are the most widespread race.

They developed martial arts, cultivation techniques, military formations, and sophisticated civilizations.

Yao

Yao are creatures that have gained intelligence and supernatural abilities through long periods of cultivation.

Some are peaceful, while others are extremely dangerous.

Spirit Beasts

Spirit Beasts are powerful supernatural animals.

Some can become companions, mounts, guardians, or enemies.

Demons

Demons originate from an ancient realm.

They possess destructive energy and often seek to expand their influence into the mortal world.

Ancient Races

Ancient Races existed long before modern civilizations.

Most have disappeared, leaving behind ruins, artifacts, and forgotten powers.

The Celestial Dragon Clan belongs to this category.

2.2 The Ancient Catastrophe

Approximately 3,000 years ago, an unknown force attacked the Celestial Dragon Clan.

The clan was nearly exterminated.

Its survivors disappeared, and its history was gradually erased.

The truth behind the catastrophe becomes the central mystery of the main storyline.

---

3. MAIN CHARACTER

3.1 Je-un (霽雲)

Age: 17
Apparent Race: Human
True Bloodline: Celestial Dragon
Starting Level: 1

Personality

- Calm and observant.
- Curious about the outside world.
- Determined when facing difficulties.
- Initially inexperienced in combat.

Starting Attributes

All attributes begin at 10.

- Strength: Physical damage.
- Vitality: Maximum health.
- Agility: Movement and attack speed.
- Endurance: Stamina and resistance.
- Spirit: Spiritual energy capacity.
- Perception: Detection and awareness.
- Willpower: Resistance to mental and spiritual attacks.

Character Development

The player can develop Je-un in several different directions:

- Sword Specialist.
- Martial Artist.
- Spear Master.
- Elemental Cultivator.
- Celestial Dragon Warrior.
- Hybrid Combatant.

There should be no mandatory single build.

---

4. CORE COMBAT SYSTEM

4.1 Player-Controlled Combat

Combat takes place in real time.

The player directly controls Je-un.

Basic Actions

- Light Attack.
- Heavy Attack.
- Charged Attack.
- Dodge.
- Block.
- Parry.
- Jump.
- Sprint.
- Lock-on.
- Special Skills.
- Ultimate Abilities.

Combat Mechanics

Attacks can be combined into different combos.

Players can interrupt enemy attacks through precise timing.

Dodging and parrying consume stamina or require timing.

Bosses have unique attack patterns and multiple combat phases.

4.2 Weapon System

Weapons determine combat style.

Weapon Categories

Sword

- Balanced attack and defense.
- Fast combos.
- Counterattacks.

Greatsword

- High damage.
- Slow attacks.
- Strong stagger potential.

Spear

- Long attack range.
- Excellent against groups.
- Strong thrust attacks.

Dual Blades

- Extremely fast attacks.
- High mobili (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

content.text:
Built a playable 3D browser game in `index.html`. It includes an explorable mountain pass, real-time combat, demon scouts and a boss, spirit-stone objectives, leveling choices, a recruitable companion, squad commands, and mobile touch controls.

Run it with `python3 -m http.server 3002` and open `http://localhost:3002`. I checked the title and gameplay views in the browser; the JavaScript syntax also passes.

Assumption: the supplied GDD excerpt ends partway through the weapon section, so I made this a focused first chapter rather than attempting to implement the full open-world scope.
